title: Interactive admin sign-in (pi.flow + PKCE)
lede: An administrator signs in through PingOne's native flow (pi.flow): this page shows the form, this app's server drives the flow, and the tokens stay on the server. Simulated in Mock.

nodes.label: Your browser
sub: This page. Never sees a token.

nodes.label: This app (server)
sub: Holds secrets and tokens, runs the safety gate, writes the audit.

edges.label: open the flow, send each step, redeem the code
a code, then the access token

steps.title: You press Sign in
steps.what: This app opens a PingOne native flow (response_mode=pi.flow) with a PKCE challenge, a nonce and the MCP server's URL as the resource (RFC 8707), and answers with the first step: the sign-in form on this page.

steps.title: You sign in on this page
steps.what: Your password goes to this app, which passes it to PingOne and does not store or log it. PingOne may ask for a one-time code (SMS or email) in the same form.

steps.title: PingOne hands back a code
steps.what: The flow completes with a one-time authorization code. There is no redirect and no callback: the browser never leaves this page.

steps.title: This app redeems the code
steps.what: This app exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier as a public client (no secret), and validates the id token's signature, issuer, audience and nonce.

steps.title: Tokens stay on the server
steps.what: Access and refresh tokens are kept on the server. The page shows only who is signed in.

steps.title: Calls carry the admin's own token
steps.what: Calls go to the hosted MCP server with the admin's own token, so the list matches that admin's roles.

steps.title: The server acts as that admin
steps.what: The server acts on the admin plane with that admin's permissions.
